firmware.statement: Student can identify the ITSboard's real hardware components (STM32F429ZI, NUCLEO-F429ZI, ITS adapter, Waveshare 4" shield) and how they connect.
Student can state the board's non-negotiable safety rules (protected pins, flash region, no mass-erase) before touching real hardware.
Student can get a working VS Code + toolchain setup for cads-zero from a clean checkout.
Student can explain why this project uses this specific ARM toolchain and build setup.
Student can build cads-zero for both the board and host-sim targets.
Student can navigate the project's module layout after a successful build.
Student can read the STM32F429ZI's memory map and locate flash/RAM/CCM regions relevant to this project.
Student can look up and use cads-zero's HAL interface for a given peripheral.
Student can flash a built firmware image to the real board via st-flash, respecting the safety rules.
Student can verify the board is running correctly after a flash using the serial console.
Student can attach GDB/st-util to a running board and inspect live state.
Student can independently complete a full build-flash-verify loop on real hardware from scratch.
Student can extend the first-build tutorial with a real conditional/gate in firmware logic.
Student can send a real UDP packet from the board using cads_net_udp_send() and verify receipt on a host.
Student can explain this project's clean-room requirement and why it constrains how code may be written.

rust.statement: Student can explain what ownership is and why Rust uses it instead of a garbage collector.
Student can use references and borrowing to use a value without taking ownership of it.
Student can use slices to reference a contiguous sequence of elements without ownership.
Student can define and instantiate a struct to group related values.
Student can explain when an enum is the right tool versus a struct.
Student can use match to handle every variant of an enum exhaustively.
Student can use if let as concise sugar for a single-pattern match.
Student can create, index, and iterate over a Vec<T>.
Student can explain why Rust strings are UTF-8 and work with String/&str correctly.
Student can use a HashMap to associate keys with values.
Student can explain when panic! is the right response to an error versus Result.
Student can propagate and handle recoverable errors using Result and the ? operator.
Student can read and write generic type parameters in a function or struct signature.
Student can define a trait and use it as a bound to constrain generic code.
Student can analyze why a borrow-checker error occurs and annotate lifetimes to resolve it.

javascript.statement: Student can explain what JavaScript is and where it runs.
Student can identify JavaScript's basic syntax, variable declarations, and primitive types.
Student can use conditionals and try/catch to control program flow and handle errors.
Student can choose and write the right loop construct for a given iteration task.
Student can define and call functions, including closures and default parameters.
Student can analyze how object properties, prototypes, and methods relate to design a small object model.
Student can use arrays and typed arrays to store and process ordered collections of data.
